title: A letter to Grandmother
intro: Sara's grandmother lives far away in Shiraz, the city of gardens, so Sara writes her a letter – and puts a drawing inside. Most of the story is the letter itself, so it practises the 'I' forms of verbs (می‌خوانم، دوست دارم), how Iranians open and close a letter, one past verb (کشیدم 'I drew') and می‌خواهم + subjunctive: می‌خواهم بیایم 'I want to come'. A week later, something comes back from Shiraz.
source: An original story for this course.

sentences.en: The letter is for her grandmother.

sentences.fa: مادربزرگ سارا در شیراز زندگی می‌کند.
sentences.r: mādar-bozorg-e Sārā dar Shirāz zendegi mi-konad.

sentences.fa: حال شما خوب است؟ من خوبم.
sentences.r: hāl-e shomā khub ast? man khub-am.

sentences.fa: من در مدرسه فارسی و ریاضی می‌خوانم.
sentences.r: man dar madrese fārsi o riyāzi mi-khānam.
sentences.en: At school I'm studying Persian and maths.

sentences.fa: دیروز یک نقاشی کشیدم: شما و من در باغ ارم!
sentences.r: diruz yek naghghāshi keshidam: shomā o man dar bāgh-e Eram!
sentences.en: Yesterday I drew a picture: you and me in the Eram Garden!
The picture is in this letter.

sentences.fa: من می‌خواهم تابستان به شیراز بیایم.
sentences.r: man mi-khāham tābestān be Shirāz bi-yāyam.
sentences.en: I want to come to Shiraz in the summer.

sentences.fa: رضا نامه را در پاکت می‌گذارد.
sentences.r: Rezā nāme rā dar pākat mi-gozārad.
sentences.en: Reza puts the letter in an envelope.

sentences.fa: سارا روی پاکت یک قلب قرمز می‌کشد.
sentences.r: Sārā ru-ye pākat yek ghalb-e ghermez mi-keshad.
sentences.en: Sara draws a red heart on the envelope.

sentences.fa: یک هفته بعد، یک نامه از شیراز می‌آید.
sentences.r: yek hafte ba'd, yek nāme az Shirāz mi-āyad.
sentences.en: A week later, a letter comes from Shiraz.

sentences.fa: در نامه یک گل خشک از باغ ارم هست.
sentences.r: dar nāme yek gol-e khoshk az bāgh-e Eram hast.
sentences.en: In the letter there is a dried flower from the Eram Garden.

questions.q: When does Sara want to go to Shiraz?

options: a letter with a dried flower

after: Persian letters often begin with a word of affection: مادربزرگ عزیزم 'my dear grandmother' – the possessive -am 'my' sits on the adjective at the end of the phrase, not on the noun. Even a child writes to her grandmother with the polite شما, because she is older. Notice the 'I' ending -am on every verb of the letter: می‌خوانم 'I study', کشیدم 'I drew', دوست دارم 'I love'. After می‌خواهم 'I want' the second verb is in the subjunctive: بیایم '(that) I come'. Shiraz is famous for its gardens, roses and poets, and باغ ارم, the Eram Garden, is one of the most beautiful gardens in Iran.
